{"id":"PKIX-77k9.2.1","title":"Finish and verify the macOS/iOS and Windows truststore backends on real toolchains","description":"pkix-truststore-system's apple.rs and windows.rs were written on 2026-11-25 and have never been compiled. Marked UNVERIFIED in the crate docs and both module headers.

What has been checked:
- They parse. rustc on each file alone reports only unresolved imports (E0432/E0433 for the absent platform crates) and no syntax errors.
- API shape matches upstream. Every call was written against signatures read out of the registry sources, not recalled: TrustSettings::new/iter, tls_trust_settings_for_certificate, SecCertificate::to_der (security-framework 3.7.0); CertStore::open_local_machine/open_current_user, CertStore::certs, CertContext::to_der (schannel 0.1.30).

What has not:
- Never type-checked. No Apple or Windows target is installed here and /usr/local/rustup is root-owned, so none could be added.
- Never run. No claim about how many anchors either returns, in what order, or what it rejects.

To do on a machine that can build them:
1. cargo check for aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Expect small breakage -- a moved import, a Result alias -- rather than a redesign.
2. Run against a real store and record the anchor count, so there is a number to notice a regression against. The host-agreement test in tests/discovery.rs is the model.
3. Windows: subtract the DISALLOWED store. The backend knowingly does not, so an administrator's explicit distrust is not honoured -- the same class of mistake the Apple backend avoids by excluding Deny trust settings. Its module documents this as a reason not to rely on it yet, and it should not be presented as finished until this is done.
4. Windows: decide what to do about auto-update roots. Modern Windows ships a small root set and fetches the rest on demand through CryptoAPI's own chain engine, so a root never yet needed on that machine is absent from the store and a chain Windows itself would complete can fail here. There may be no fix from outside the chain engine, in which case document it as a limitation.
5. Consider whether the Apple backend should keep iterating System/Admin/User in that order. pkix-truststore does not deduplicate, so the order decides which copy survives when domains hold the same certificate in different encodings.

The portable bundle/directory reader works on both platforms and is tested, so a consumer on macOS or Windows who needs something dependable can set SSL_CERT_FILE or install a bundle today. This is a quality gap, not a blocker.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T19:03:55.016038036Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T19:03:55.016038036Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"PKIX-77k9.2.1","depends_on_id":"PKIX-77k9.2","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-25T19:03:55.216047896Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
new_value: {"notes":"macOS and Windows are verified as of 2026-11-25. .github/workflows/platform-truststore.yml compiles and runs the crate on macos-latest and windows-latest on every change to it; from_system reports Source::Native and returns a non-empty anchor set on both, with --nocapture in the step so a skipped assertion cannot be read as a passing one. Shipped as pkix-truststore-system 0.2.0.\n\nRemaining for this bead: iOS and Android. iOS shares src/apple.rs but not its entitlements and has no runner; Android has neither. Also still open regardless of platform: the Windows backend does not subtract the DISALLOWED store, and anchor counts/ordering/rejections are unmeasured on every platform because a runner's trust store is not a user's."}
